result.paraphrase:
We present a polynomial-time algorithm that achieves a 3/2+ε approximation guarantee for the s-t-path TSP, for every fixed ε > 0.

As is well known, Wolsey’s analysis of Christofide’s algorithm extends to the s-t-path TSP under its standard LP relaxation, except for narrow cuts, where the LP optimum is below two. For a fixed optimal tour, each narrow cut is either crossed by exactly one edge—making both the edge and the cut lonely—or by at least three edges, in which case the cut is busy. Our method uses dynamic programming to guess the lonely cuts and edges, then splits the problem into smaller subinstances and tightens the LP by insisting that every busy cut has value at least three. With a k-stage recursive dynamic program, we can find a spanning tree (V, S) and an LP solution y such that (½ + O(2−k)) y lies in the T-join polyhedron, where T is the set of vertices whose degree in S has the wrong parity.
